prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1296; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a left-turn collision at an intersection involving a concussion injury. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy declarations and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is listed as a named driver. Coverage was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle at the scene and matches the account given in the first notice of loss. Nothing in the report suggests the damage predates the policy period.

Entry 4: Statements from two independent witnesses describe the other vehicle turning across the claimant's path, consistent with the sequence in the claimant's account. The other driver has also confirmed the events as described.

Entry 5: Photographs of the vehicles were reviewed. The damage pattern to the front quarter panel and passenger door lines up well with the impact described, and no older damage has been identified on either vehicle.

Entry 6: Medical records show a concussion diagnosis with symptoms consistent with the force of a side impact of this type. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the file has been flagged for a closer look at the treatment timeline.

Entry 7: Searched prior claims and available medical history. No earlier injury to the same body area is on record, and no prior claims involving the claimant's head or neck have been found.

Entry 8: Claimant's counsel provided a follow-up statement adding a few minor details about the moments before impact. The core account is unchanged from the original report, and the additions do not conflict with the witness statements or photographs.

Entry 9: Reserves reviewed in light of the medical timeline and the consistent liability picture. File remains open pending the treating physician's final report, with the next review scheduled after that report is received.
